clue.text: Illicit tool criminal concealed in sponge

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the word before it is twisted into a new order
what is concealed in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to sponge is to cadge or beg
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy implement hidden away inside a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods are made or sold unlawfully, originally smuggled liquor, so the word is an adjective meaning unlawful.

clue.text: Solemn type enters competition to claim a wicket

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: a bout is a contest, as in boxing
an owl is proverbially solemn-looking and wise

explanation.surface: A serious character joins a cricket match intending to take a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler dismisses a batter by hitting the stumps behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, to bowl someone out is to dismiss the batter, which credits the bowler with taking their wicket.

clue.text: Indecent old book site

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
B is the abbreviation for book
the scene of a crime is its site

explanation.surface: A website hosting a rude old book.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material offends against accepted standards of decency, so the two words are near synonyms for offensive content.

clue.text: Tarzan's means of getting around a pin-up?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a nail is a metal pin for fastening

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Tarzan travels about with the aid of a poster or a drawing pin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pin-up looks like a poster, but the hyphen hides a word followed by the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan swings through the jungle on long woody climbing vines, which is exactly what these tropical creepers are.

clue.text: Western female at border with oil rich peninsula

indicators.note: a rich mixture is a blended one, so the letters of the word before it are stirred up

blocks.note: gal is the folksy word for a girl in a cowboy Western
the lip of a cup is its rim
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman from the American West living on the frontier of an oilfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Oil rich reads as one phrase about wealth, but rich is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli is the Turkish peninsula on the Dardanelles, site of the disastrous 1915 Allied campaign.

clue.text: Stomach-churning musical great

indicators.note: churning stirs things about, so the letters of the word before it are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer so brilliant that hearing them makes your insides turn over.
explanation.walkthrough: Satchmo was the nickname of the jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong, known by this nickname, was one of the towering figures of jazz trumpet and singing.

clue.text: Brat presenting second short broadcast

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its tail end

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a broadcast is a radio or television programme

explanation.surface: A child star hosting a brief second transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: Prog is the everyday clipped form; sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a child, and a brat is a badly behaved child.

clue.text: Casual and tense, by chance? That's to invite bad luck

blocks.note: a casual is a temporary worker
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
fate is what chance deals out

explanation.surface: Being relaxed and nervous at the same time is asking for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Casual and tense look like a pair of contrasting adjectives; casual is a noun for a stand-in worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt fate is to act rashly in a way that seems to dare misfortune to strike.

clue.text: Accessory of workman getting the sack

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: A labourer's belongings as he is fired from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting the sack suggests dismissal, but the sack simply means a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbag is a fashion item carried with an outfit, so it counts as a clothing accessory.

clue.text: Public welcomes each cut? Get stuffed!

indicators.note: someone who welcomes a guest takes them in, so one word goes inside
a word that is cut is shortened, losing its end

blocks.note: overt means open and in public view
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A town hall greeting every budget cut, met with a rude retort.
explanation.walkthrough: Get stuffed! looks like a dismissive insult but is a literal instruction to eat too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To get stuffed literally is to eat until bloated, so as an imperative it tells someone to gorge themselves.

clue.text: Keen to restrict Neddy's revelry

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: to keen is to lament loudly
Neddy is a familiar name for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey eagerly penned in while a party goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Neddy stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is old-fashioned festive drinking and merrymaking, especially at Christmas, so it names boisterous celebration.

clue.text: Court can, if reconstituted in the capital

indicators.note: something reconstituted is rebuilt from its parts, so the short word is put back together in a different order
placing one thing in another means it is enclosed by the second

blocks.note: the capital city of Italy, the classic crossword capital
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of a tin rebuilt in the city, as if recycling were a civic project.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them, which as a verb is what it means to romance a person.

clue.text: Working with board that supports constitutional procedures

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'the thing that supports', with board doing double duty

blocks.note: a machine that is working is running or functioning
a board is a flat table top, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone serving on a committee board that oversees constitutional matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The word board does double duty, giving the second part and heading the definition. Constitutional here means relating to the body's constitution, so the procedures are surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons operate on a patient lying on this flat padded platform, the bodily procedures being what the definition calls constitutional.

clue.text: See 11
Material leak covered up by discontented tabloid

indicators.note: without its contents a word keeps only its outside, so just the first and last letters stay
something covered up by another is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: the outermost letters of the word
to leak, in slang, is to urinate

explanation.surface: A grumpy red-top newspaper burying a story that someone leaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, so the answer is a specific kind of fabric used for jackets and suits.

clue.text: Inclination to pass on ground wheat dish

indicators.note: grain that is ground is broken up, so the letters following are crushed and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to refuse a plate of milled cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass on looks like declining food; here it means to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A death wish is a conscious or unconscious desire to die, and passing on is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Ill, Mark's failing to meet objective

blocks.note: feeling off means feeling unwell
a mark is something aimed at

explanation.surface: A man named Mark falls sick and so misses his goals.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name; the 's after it stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that is wide of its aim has missed, so being astray of the goal means not reaching an objective.

clue.text: Hot air from this nut with an old gun

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a football nut
heater is old gangster slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Pompous talk from a crackpot brandishing an antique firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot air suggests empty boasting, but here it is literally warm air blown out by an appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: This electric appliance blows warmed air into a room with a fan, so hot air comes out of it.

clue.text: Outline something commonly associated with moon (new)

blocks.note: commonly signals a dialect form; summat is northern English for something
Io is one of Jupiter's moons
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A vague remark about the moon, with a bracketed reminder that it is a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: Moon is not a general word for satellite here; it names one specific moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A summation sums up the main points, so it is a summary sketch of the whole argument.

clue.text: Orange-yellow shifts for fans

indicators.note: shifting moves things around, so the letters of the words either side are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Bright coloured shirts sold to supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Shifts looks like a noun for loose dresses or work periods, but it is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron names the deep golden colour of the spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Gag writer's ultimate neckwear

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to gag someone is to muffle them
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comedy writer's best joke turns out to be a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag reads as a joke for a comedy writer but is a verb meaning silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffler is an old-fashioned word for a warm woollen scarf wrapped round the neck.

clue.text: Barge below rocks

indicators.note: rocking shakes things about, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A canal boat sitting beneath some rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Barge looks like a noun for a boat but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge through a crowd is to shove past people, which is to elbow one's way through.

clue.text: Maybe Brian's not so great in the sack

indicators.note: placing a word in another means it is surrounded by the second

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack
less is smaller or not as much

explanation.surface: Someone named Brian turns out to be a disappointing lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Blessed is a booming British actor; maybe signals that Brian is one example of a person with this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition gives an example: the actor Brian Blessed bears this surname, so he is one of the people so called.

clue.text: Evidence of liquid nitrogen in contaminated sweets

indicators.note: contaminated stuff is spoiled and disordered, so the letters of the word after it are scrambled
one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Lab tests find liquid nitrogen tainting a batch of confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquid nitrogen reads as one coolant; liquid belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampness on a surface shows that water or some other fluid has been there.

clue.text: Not wanting to incriminate myself I take it?

definitions.text: Not wanting to incriminate myself I take it?

blocks.clueFragment: Not wanting to incriminate myself I take it?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone accepting something, perhaps a plea or a drink, to avoid self-incrimination

blocks.clueFragment: Not wanting to incriminate myself I take it?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the US constitutional protection a witness invokes by saying they take it in court

explanation.walkthrough: In American courts a witness who refuses to answer says 'I take the Fifth', invoking the constitutional right against self-incrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: This article of the US Bill of Rights protects anyone from being compelled to testify against themselves in criminal proceedings.

clue.text: See 22
One needs to blend honey

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
ingredients that gel come together and blend

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to stir in some honey.
explanation.walkthrough: Honey looks like a food ingredient but is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate terms for a loved one, used when addressing a sweetheart or darling.

clue.text: Comparatively boring towel?

blocks.note: first meaning: duller, as with a speech that is more tedious
second meaning: a thing that removes moisture

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one bath towel is duller than another.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of dry means more tedious, and a towel is a thing that dries you after washing.

clue.text: Staggeringly rich?

definitions.note: adverb in the clue; the answer is the adjective, as in a rolling gait

blocks.note: first meaning: lurching from side to side, as a drunk walks
second meaning: informal for very wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone astonishingly wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Staggeringly looks like an intensifier for rich, but it is a separate meaning: a staggering, swaying gait.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling walk sways unsteadily like a drunk's, and someone rolling in it has money to spare.

clue.text: Taxes on the vacated port

indicators.note: a vacated place has had its occupants removed, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: something that taxes you tries your patience
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Duties levied on a harbour that has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: Taxes is a verb meaning strains, not a noun for duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major seaport city in north-east Italy on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Marine creature managed to turn over by itself almost

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word is read from end to start
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense
itself refers back to the marine creature, which is a kind of whale

explanation.surface: A sea animal that somehow flipped itself over unaided.
explanation.walkthrough: Itself is self-referential: the creature being defined is a small Arctic whale, so the word stands for that.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic toothed whale whose males carry a long spiral tusk, so it is a sea animal.

clue.text: Screen made of reeds or bananas

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A partition woven from rushes, or else from banana leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas reads as part of the materials list but is the signal for mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental partition or panel standing behind a church altar.
